test_title: RRB NTPC - Graduate 2025 (CBT 2) Foundational Full Test - 02
subject: general
question:
With reference to the Global Methane Pledge, consider the following statements:

I. The pledge was announced during the COP26 climate conference.

II. It aims to achieve a substantial reduction in global methane emissions by 2030 compared to 2020 levels.

III. India is a formal signatory to this pledge.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
solution:
The correct answer is **Option B**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Global Methane Pledge** is a voluntary international initiative aimed at addressing **methane emissions**, a potent short-lived climate pollutant.
 
• The pledge was **announced during the COP26 climate conference (Glasgow, 2021)** as a joint initiative led by the United States and the European Union. Hence, **Statement I is correct**.
 
• It seeks to achieve a **global reduction of methane emissions by at least 30% by 2030**, taking **2020 levels as the baseline**. Hence, **Statement II is correct**.
 
• **India is not a formal signatory** to the Global Methane Pledge, citing concerns related to its **agriculture sector and development priorities**. Hence, **Statement III is incorrect**.
 
• **Thus, only two statements (I and II) are correct → Option B. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Methane has a **much higher warming potential than carbon dioxide** over a 20-year time horizon.
 
• Major global sources of methane include **agriculture (especially livestock), fossil fuel extraction, and waste management**.
 
• While not legally binding, the pledge encourages **national action plans, technological cooperation, and monitoring** to curb methane emissions.
